name: Reel Segment Ideation Board
use_when: A short-form edit needs polished motion graphics but the agent must decide what each segment should show first.
The rough cut has clear spoken segments created by trims or sentence beats.
The editor needs to batch multiple reels efficiently for a creator or client.
A scripted video needs sentence-level planning for screen recordings, images, videos, text, overlays, and animations.
avoid_when: The source is a simple clip that only needs captions and minor trimming.
The user explicitly wants improvisational visual exploration before a plan.
The segment plan would over-explain a hook that should stay simple.

timeline_pattern.pattern: prepared_cut -> segment_boundaries -> visual_support_choice -> rough_sketch_or_note -> asset_list -> animation_pass
timeline_pattern.support_options: For each segment choose: captions only, speaker plus text, on-screen animation, full-screen animation, B-roll/image, icon/proof, or no added visual.
timeline_pattern.batch_rule: When multiple reels are coming, batch similar work: prepare all cuts, ideate all segments, gather assets, then animate.
timeline_pattern.message_rule: Every segment visual must make the message easier to understand, not just make the timeline busier.
timeline_pattern.script_color_rule: For scripted work, color-code or tag each sentence by visual category before gathering assets.

motion.rule: Choose animation complexity by message value: simple text for small beats, full-screen/camera scenes for major explanations.

sound.rule: Leave SFX/music decisions until the segment visuals and motion beats are known.

captions.rule: Flag segments where captions should be suppressed because visual text already carries the idea.

color.rule: Use ideation to preserve one style system across segment backgrounds, icons, and text.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use segment metadata with start/end times, spoken text summary, visualSupport, assetsNeeded, and captionSuppression flags.
implementation.remotion: Store segment plans as data objects that choose components such as CaptionOnly, SpeakerText, FullscreenScene, IconPath, ScreenRecord, ImageBeat, or CTA.
implementation.blender: Storyboard camera-heavy or 3D segments before building scenes.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Mark segment beats, write a quick visual plan, gather assets, then build templates only for the segments that need them.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use markers or sequence notes for each trimmed segment before sending a prepared render to After Effects; for scripted YouTube edits, mirror the script color tags in bins and timeline markers.

common_mistakes: Opening After Effects before knowing what each spoken segment should communicate.
Adding assets to the screen because they look premium rather than because they explain the segment.
Using the same complexity level for every line.
Forgetting to list required icons, images, or proof assets before animation.
Animating captions and visual text that say the same thing.
Color-coding the script but failing to gather the matching assets before editing.
qc: Does each segment have a visual support decision before animation begins?
Can every visual be tied to a spoken concept or proof need?
Are required assets listed before the animation pass starts?
Does the segment plan preserve one coherent style system?
Do script color tags match the assets and timeline layers?
